_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present
entries.usage: Now or regularly.
entries.example: Ik speel voetbal.

entries.label: zijn (present)
entries.usage: 'to be'.
entries.example: Ik ben moe.

entries.label: hebben (present)
entries.usage: 'to have'.
entries.example: Ik heb tijd.

entries.point: The perfect: heb gewerkt, ben gegaan
entries.label: Perfect
entries.usage: Finished past with hebben/zijn.
entries.example: Ik heb gewerkt.

entries.label: Imperfect
entries.usage: The narrative/written past.
entries.example: Ik speelde vaak buiten.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: Ik ga morgen komen.

entries.point: Modal verbs: kunnen, moeten, mogen, willen
entries.label: Modal verbs
entries.usage: can/must/may/want + infinitive.
entries.example: Ik kan zwemmen.

entries.label: Imperative
entries.usage: Commands.
entries.example: Kom hier!

entries.point: Progressive: aan het + infinitive, zitten te
entries.label: Progressive
entries.usage: Happening right now.
entries.example: Ik ben aan het eten.

entries.point: Separable verbs: opstaan → ik sta op
entries.label: Separable verbs
entries.usage: The prefix splits off to the end.
entries.example: Ik sta om zeven uur op.

entries.point: Word order: the verb comes second
entries.label: Verb second
entries.usage: In an ordinary statement the verb stays in second place, even when the sentence opens with a time or a place.
entries.example: Morgen ga ik naar Amsterdam. — Tomorrow I am going to Amsterdam.

entries.label: niet / geen
entries.usage: Saying no: geen cancels a thing you don't have, niet cancels everything else.
entries.example: Ik heb geen auto. — I don't have a car.

entries.label: Questions
entries.usage: Asking something: put the verb in front of the person, or open with a question word.
entries.example: Waar woon je? — Where do you live?

entries.label: Er is / zijn
entries.usage: Saying that something exists or is around, and asking whether there is any.
entries.example: Er is een probleem. — There is a problem.

entries.point: Subclauses: the verb walks to the end
entries.label: Verb last
entries.usage: In the half of a sentence that starts with omdat, dat or als, the verb drops to the very end.
entries.example: Ik blijf thuis omdat ik ziek ben. — I'm staying home because I am sick.

entries.label: Om te
entries.usage: Saying what you are doing something for.
entries.example: Ik ga naar de markt om groente te kopen. — I'm going to the market to buy vegetables.

entries.point: Reflexive verbs: zich vergissen, zich voelen
entries.label: Reflexive verbs
entries.usage: When the action comes back to the person doing it, and with verbs that always demand it.
entries.example: Ik vergis me soms. — I am sometimes mistaken.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: When what was done matters more than who did it.
entries.example: De weg wordt volgende week gerepareerd. — The road will be repaired next week.

entries.point: Want vs omdat, dus and maar
entries.label: want / omdat
entries.usage: Giving a reason — and the word you choose decides where the verb goes.
entries.example: Ik blijf thuis, want ik ben ziek. — I'm staying home, for I am sick.

entries.point: Te + infinitive: proberen te, hoeven te
entries.label: proberen te / hoeven te
entries.usage: Hooking a second verb onto verbs like proberen, hoeven and beloven.
entries.example: Ik probeer elke dag te sporten. — I try to exercise every day.

entries.label: zou (would)
entries.usage: Asking politely, imagining something, giving advice, or passing on what people say.
entries.example: Zou je het raam kunnen sluiten? — Could you close the window?

entries.label: Indirect speech
entries.usage: Reporting what somebody said or asked instead of quoting them.
entries.example: Hij zegt dat hij morgen komt. — He says that he is coming tomorrow.

entries.point: Modal particles: wel, toch, maar, even, eens
entries.label: wel / toch / maar
entries.usage: The small words that soften, nudge or gently contradict, and make you sound Dutch.
entries.example: Het is wel lekker, hoor. — It IS actually tasty.

entries.label: Past perfect (had gedaan)
entries.usage: Telling about something that was already finished before another past moment.
entries.example: Ik had al gegeten toen zij kwam. — I had already eaten when she came.

entries.label: Double infinitives
entries.usage: Putting can, must or want into the past with heb or had.
entries.example: Ik heb vannacht niet kunnen slapen. — I couldn't sleep last night.

entries.label: Conditionals
entries.usage: Talking about what happens, would happen, or would have happened if something is true.
entries.example: Als ik rijk was, zou ik de wereld rondreizen. — If I were rich, I would travel the world.

entries.point: The tang: brackets around the sentence
entries.label: Verb bracket
entries.usage: In sentences with two verb parts, everything else sits packed between them.
entries.example: Ik heb gisteren de hele dag aan mijn scriptie gewerkt. — I worked on my thesis all day yesterday.

entries.point: Posture verbs as 'to be': staan, liggen, zitten
entries.label: Posture verbs
entries.usage: Saying where a thing is — Dutch says it stands, lies or sits there.
entries.example: De fles staat op tafel. — The bottle is (standing) on the table.

entries.point: De and het: the two genders
entries.label: De / het
entries.usage: The two article genders.
entries.example: de man, het huis

entries.label: Adjective -e
entries.usage: When the adjective takes -e.
entries.example: een rode auto, het rode huis

entries.label: Plurals
entries.usage: Noun plural forms.
entries.example: boek → boeken, auto → auto's

entries.label: Possessives
entries.usage: my/your/his/her.
entries.example: mijn broer, haar boek

entries.label: Comparative
entries.usage: -er / -st.
entries.example: groot → groter → grootst

entries.label: Diminutives
entries.usage: The -je ending (little / cute).
entries.example: huis → huisje

entries.point: Subject pronouns: ik, jij, u, hij, zij…
entries.label: Subject pronouns
entries.usage: Naming who is doing something — I, you, he, she, we, they — with a polite you as well.
entries.example: Jij komt uit Nederland, hij komt uit België. — You are from the Netherlands, he is from Belgium.

entries.point: Er — the five jobs of one little word
entries.label: er (five jobs)
entries.usage: Standing in for a place already mentioned, an amount, or a thing after a small word like over.
entries.example: Hoeveel katten heb je? — Ik heb er twee. — How many cats do you have? — I have two (of them).

entries.label: die / dat
entries.usage: Adding extra information about a thing: de-words take die, het-words take dat.
entries.example: De vrouw die daar staat, is mijn buurvrouw. — The woman who is standing there is my neighbour.

entries.label: waarover / ermee
entries.usage: Saying about it, with it or in it — and asking what about.
entries.example: Waar denk je aan? — What are you thinking about?

entries.label: u or je
entries.usage: Choosing between polite u and everyday je, in speech and in letters.
entries.example: Kunt u mij even helpen? — Could you help me for a moment? (to a friend: kun je me even helpen?)

entries.label: Making nouns
entries.usage: Turning a verb or a quality into a thing you can talk about.
entries.example: Het reizen verbreedt de blik. — Travelling broadens the mind.

entries.point: Netherlands vs Flanders: one language, two flavours
entries.label: Dutch vs Flemish
entries.usage: Which words and forms you hear in Belgium rather than in the Netherlands.
entries.example: Ik heb goesting in frieten. — I fancy fries. (in the Netherlands: Ik heb zin in patat.)

entries.point: Fossils: der, des, te allen tijde
entries.label: Old case forms
entries.usage: Set phrases and formal writing that kept endings everyday Dutch dropped.
entries.example: Dat is nu eenmaal de loop der dingen. — That is simply the way of things.
